title: llm-proxy configuration (v0)
description: The simple, LLM-native configuration dialect for llm-proxy. This file is the single source of truth for the v0 schema: user-facing documentation, editor autocomplete (yaml-language-server), and the config validator are all generated from it. The dialect is a front-end: it compiles ('lowers') to standard Envoy resources and runs through the exact same validation pipeline as Envoy bootstrap config — `llm-proxy config translate` shows the generated Envoy configuration. Strings support environment-variable interpolation with `${VAR_NAME}`, applied before parsing. Parsing is strict: unknown fields are errors, never ignored. Advanced needs beyond this dialect: use Envoy bootstrap mode (`-c bootstrap.yaml`). The top-level keys `envoy`, `tracing`, and `clusters` are RESERVED for future versions and rejected in v0.

version.description: Schema version. Must be 0. Future schema revisions bump this; llm-proxy refuses configs whose version it does not understand.

listen.description: Where the proxy accepts client traffic. Shorthand string `host:port`, or an object to enable TLS. Default: `0.0.0.0:8080` (plaintext).

admin.description: Admin/observability endpoint (`/ready`, `/stats/prometheus`, `/config_dump`). Disabled when omitted. Bind to loopback unless you know why not.

providers.description: Named upstream LLM API providers. The key is the provider name referenced by `routes` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Names `openai` and `anthropic` infer their `type` and `base_url` automatically — a working OpenAI provider is just `openai: { api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY} }`.

routes.description: Ordered routing rules, evaluated top to bottom — the FIRST rule whose `model` pattern matches the request wins (there is no specificity reordering; put specific patterns above broad ones). Requests matching no rule get a 404 with a JSON error body listing known models.

limits.description: Rate limits and quotas, enforced before a request is forwarded (over-limit requests get a 429 with `x-ratelimit-*` headers). Token counts are extracted from provider responses (streaming included). NOTE: limits are enforced per proxy instance in v0; fleet-wide limits require the (future) shared budget store.

observability.description: Metrics and access logging. Prometheus metrics (including token counters, TTFT/TPOT histograms, per-model dimensions) are always computed and exposed on the admin endpoint when `admin` is configured.

HostPort.description: A bind address in `host:port` form. IPv6 hosts use brackets: `[::1]:8080`.

Duration.description: A duration: integer plus unit — `ms` (milliseconds), `s` (seconds), `m` (minutes), or `h` (hours).

TokenAmount.description: A token count: a plain integer, or a string with `k` (thousands) / `m` (millions) suffix.

ModelPattern.description: A glob matched against the request's `model` field (the JSON body field for chat/completions APIs; the `model` query parameter for realtime WebSocket endpoints). `*` matches any run of characters; matching is case-sensitive. `*` alone matches every request.

ProviderModelRef.description: A provider reference: `provider-name` (keep the request's model name) or `provider-name/model-name` (rewrite the model before forwarding, e.g. fall back from `gpt-5` to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`).

tls.description: Terminate TLS for client connections. Certificate files are watched and hot-reloaded on change — no restart needed for renewal.

cert_file.description: Path to the PEM certificate chain.

key_file.description: Path to the PEM private key.

Provider.description: One upstream LLM API. Exactly one of `api_key` / `api_key_file` may be set (omit both for unauthenticated local backends).

type.description: Provider API shape. `openai-compatible` covers vLLM, Ollama, TGI, Together, and most self-hosted servers. Inferred for providers named `openai` or `anthropic`; defaults to `openai-compatible` otherwise.

base_url.description: API base URL. Required unless the provider name/type implies one (`openai` -> https://api.openai.com, `anthropic` -> https://api.anthropic.com).

api_key.description: API key, sent using the provider type's native auth header (`Authorization: Bearer` for OpenAI-shaped APIs, `x-api-key` for Anthropic). Use `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation rather than inlining secrets.

api_key_file.description: Read the API key from this file (trailing whitespace trimmed; watched and hot-reloaded). Preferred over `api_key` for secret managers that mount files.

extra_headers.description: Additional headers to send on every request to this provider (e.g. `anthropic-version`, org/project headers).

ca_file.description: PEM CA bundle for verifying this provider's TLS certificate. Only needed for self-hosted backends with private CAs; system roots are used otherwise.

connect_timeout.description: TCP/TLS connection establishment timeout for this provider.

provider.description: Where matching requests go. `provider/model` form rewrites the model name before forwarding.

fallbacks.description: Tried in order when the primary provider fails (connection failure, 429, or 5xx — and never after the first response byte of a stream has been sent to the client). Each fallback gets a fresh attempt with the same request body, model-rewritten if the `provider/model` form is used.

retries.description: Retry policy against the SAME provider, applied before moving to `fallbacks`. Defaults are LLM-safe: retry only what is certainly unserved (connection failures, 429s, and 5xx received before any response byte); a request is never replayed once streaming to the client has begun.

attempts.description: Extra attempts against the primary provider (0 disables retries).

idle_timeout.description: Maximum time with NO bytes flowing (between response chunks / SSE events / WebSocket frames). There is deliberately no total-duration timeout by default — LLM generations and realtime sessions are long-lived; idle-based timeouts are the correct guard.

key.description: What the limit is counted against: `global` (one bucket for all traffic), `client-ip` (one bucket per client address), or `header:<name>` (one bucket per distinct value of the named request header — e.g. `header:x-api-key` for per-caller quotas).

tokens_per_minute.description: Total (input + output) tokens allowed per minute per bucket. Usage is extracted from provider responses, including streamed ones; enforcement is at request admission (the request that would exceed the budget is rejected — in-flight streams are never truncated).

requests_per_minute.description: Requests allowed per minute per bucket.

concurrent_sessions.description: Maximum simultaneous long-lived sessions (WebSocket realtime connections and active SSE streams) per bucket. Enforced at connection/upgrade time — the 429 happens before the session starts, never mid-session.

models.description: Restrict this limit to requests whose model matches one of these patterns. Omit to apply to all traffic.

access_logs.description: Where and how per-request/per-session access log entries are written.

output.description: `stdout`, `stderr`, or a file path. Streamed responses and realtime sessions are logged once at stream end with usage totals.

format.description: `json` emits one structured object per line (recommended for log pipelines).
